description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is an open reasoning supervised fine-tuning dataset of 1.2 million question-response pairs spanning math, code, and science. It is built through a pipeline that sources questions from selected datasets, filters questions, applies deduplication for math and science, samples 16 answers per question from a teacher model, and releases the resulting data for training reasoning models.
name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
rai:annotationsPerItem: 16 answers per question in the final pipeline.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper evaluates alternative annotation and filtering strategies through controlled ablations across math, code, and science, including teacher-model comparisons and answer filtering experiments. It reports downstream benchmark performance and standard errors for these strategies.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions are sourced from selected datasets, filtered for quality, optionally deduplicated, then answered by a teacher model to create reasoning traces and final answers. The final OpenThoughts3 pipeline uses QwQ-32B as teacher, 16 answers per question, exact deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code, and no answer filtering.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes a design tradeoff between source quality and diversity, finding that selecting only one or two top-performing sources works better than mixing many sources. It also notes that the final strategy optimizes overall average benchmark performance rather than each domain individually, assuming cross-domain transfer, and that performance may depend strongly on the nature and quality of question sources.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is collected by sourcing questions from existing public datasets and newly generated sources across math, code, and science, then filtering questions, deduplicating some domains, sampling questions, and generating responses with a teacher model. The final dataset contains 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of source questions drawn from existing datasets and programmatically generated sources. The final pipeline uses OpenMath-2-Math for math; StackExchange CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code; and StackExchange Physics and OrganicChemistryPDFs for science.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis, User-generated content data, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes several limitations: it does not explore reinforcement learning datasets, staged supervised fine-tuning, or curriculum learning; some benchmarks saturate or do not respond to scale; and questions remain about cross-domain transfer and whether scaling continues to help as student models approach teacher performance.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection processing includes filtering questions with LLM-based methods, deduplicating math and science questions by exact match, randomly sampling questions, generating 16 answers per question, decontaminating against evaluation benchmarks using indel similarity and n-gram overlap, and choosing not to perform answer filtering in the final pipeline.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset pipeline filters sourced questions, performs exact deduplication for math and science, randomly samples questions, generates multiple answers per question, and decontaminates training data against evaluation sets using normalized indel similarity and n-gram similarity. For some source creation steps, OCR and question extraction/refinement are applied to PDF documents.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The project aims to make reasoning model training more open by releasing public datasets and models instead of relying on proprietary data. The paper also notes safety concerns: improved reasoning performance can degrade safety alignment, and future work should incorporate safety-specific datasets.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for supervised fine-tuning of reasoning models, particularly for math, code, and science reasoning. It is used to train OpenThinker3-7B and is presented as an open-source resource for building and studying reasoning models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen/QwQ-32B is the final teacher model used to generate answers. The pipeline also uses DeepSeek-R1 in experiments, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini/4.1-nano for question filtering and other automated judgments, fastText classifiers for filtering, text-embedding-3-large for embedding-based selection, gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 for PDF OCR, and Evalchemy for evaluation.
